blocks.source: Vol IV, Adversarial Verification, § Fault Oracles and Acceptance
blocks.md: A valid verification trace for the F1 safety claim must establish both timely deceleration onset and bounded stopping distance; observing that the robot base eventually stopped establishes neither guarantee. Without an oracle fixed in advance, post-hoc inspection takes over: engineers eyeball time-series plots after the run, seizing on gross symptoms such as whether Joule heating melted a motor phase wire or a controller threw an unhandled exception. The trial degenerates into an anecdote.

questions.q: The section **Fault Oracles and Acceptance** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A transduction attack delivers a checksum-valid packet whose measurement is false, so packet integrity is never an oracle for perception, and a wrong action inside the envelope after prompt injection or a patch is a coverage deficit, never a pass.
A fault trial counts as evidence only against an oracle fixed before the run that returns signed margins, scored from the event the fault disrupts rather than from the start of the trial.
Extreme value theory fits the distribution of block maxima or threshold exceedances, so a tail estimate needs many independent extremes and a justified tail family.
Signed temporal-logic robustness turns testing into an optimization that searches for the smallest margin, and a simulated margin counts only after its sim-to-real transfer discount.
